title: Mboume (Névadaye), Moringa-Leaf Sauce
author: chef Bineta Diallo Dioh (Slow Food Foundation / FAO)
desc: Moringa leaves steeped two minutes in boiling water to take out the bitterness, then cooked 40 minutes with raw ground peanut flour, meat, dried fish, cherry tomatoes and tomato paste until the sauce thickens and the peanut oil floats.
longDesc: A thick leaf sauce from the Slow Food Foundation and FAO’s Senegal booklet of traditional products and dishes (‘de la terre à la table’), with recipes credited to chef Bineta Diallo Dioh. The moringa leaves, dried or fresh, are steeped in boiling water for two minutes to remove bitterness and drained; they go into a pot with 500 g of raw peanut flour, 500 g of meat, 150 g of dried fish, 100 g of cherry tomatoes, 50 g of tomato paste and an onion, and cook 40 minutes. The printed cue is that at the end of cooking the sauce becomes thick and the peanut oil floats to the surface. It is served with couscous, millet or maize.
ingredients: Dried or fresh moringa leaves — quantity not printed
Salt, pepper and chilli (optional) — quantities not printed
steps: Steep the moringa leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes to remove bitterness, then drain.
Put the meat, the leaves and all the other ingredients in a pot and cook for 40 minutes, then add salt.
Lower the heat and adjust the seasoning. At the end of cooking the sauce should be thick and the peanut oil should float on the surface.
Serve with couscous, millet or maize.
chefTips: The printed doneness cue: the sauce thickens and the peanut oil rises to the surface.
The two-minute steep removes the bitterness of the leaves.
The page prints no pot size or amount of water; add water as needed to keep the sauce from catching.
commonMistakes: Adding salt before the end of the 40 minutes — the page salts after cooking.
reheating: Warm gently, adding a little water.
healthBenefits: Moringa leaves are rich in iron, vitamin A and calcium.
culturalNote: The booklet notes moringa originated near the Himalayas and has been present in Africa since the end of ancient Egypt. No region or ethnic group is stated for this recipe.
sources: Source: ‘Sénégal — produits et plats traditionnels / de la terre à la table’, Slow Food Foundation for Biodiversity with FAO (project GTF/RAF/426/ITA); directed by Velia Lucidi and Serena Milano; texts Serena Berisio; recipes credited to chef Bineta Diallo Dioh; translation and editing Pierre Le Chevallier. No publication date printed. Fetched at two independent URLs (fao.org and fondazioneslowfood.com), quantities identical — TWO-PASS.

Yield: ‘Pour 10 personnes’. Local names as printed: ‘Mboume’; ‘Névadaye’. Cue, direct quote: ‘En fin de cuisson, la sauce devient épaisse et l’huile de l’arachide surnage.’ No temperature printed. The prep and cook figures are 2 minutes of steeping plus 40 minutes cooking, as printed; the prep figure is a scheduling estimate.
ABSENT, not estimated: moringa quantity; salt, pepper and chilli amounts.
